title: Geometric quantification for nonlinear deformation in knitted fabrics
summary: Knitted fabrics exemplify a broad class of architected materials capable of large deformations, enabling shape morphing, mechanical biocompatibility, and embedded multifunctionality without material damage. Although geometric nonlinearity has been intuitively utilized in their design, a quantitative description of stitch-resolved deformation and its temporal evolution remains lacking.
